# CliFn

> Reusable CLI building blocks for command execution, output, configuration, credentials, and safe automation.

This file concatenates the full text of every documentation page so it can be loaded into
an LLM-based assistant in a single shot. For a page index, see /docs/llms.txt.

# Documentation

<!-- page:docs:automation.md path:/docs/automation -->
# Subprocesses and scaffolding

> Execute commands and create files with explicit limits and overwrite policy.


`@clifn/core/exec` exports `createExec()`. Call `command(file, args, options)` with a separate executable and argument array. The result includes command, exit code or signal, captured stdout and stderr, timeout state, and duration. Capture defaults to one MiB per stream; set `maxBufferBytes` to change it. Output beyond the limit is dropped from the captured `stdout`/`stderr` without an error or flag, although streaming callbacks still receive every chunk. Timeout defaults to 30 seconds. Pass callbacks or `streamOutput` to observe chunks while the command runs.

```ts
import { createExec } from "@clifn/core/exec";

const result = await createExec().command("git", ["status", "--short"], {
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  timeoutMs: 10_000,
});
if (result.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
```

On timeout, `ExecTimeoutError` carries code `CLIFN_EXEC_TIMEOUT` and the partial result. The child receives SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a short grace period. `runAction()` exposes this service as `ctx.exec` with inherited working directory and environment.

`@clifn/core/scaffold` exports `createScaffold()`. Its `apply()` accepts `mkdir` and `write-file` operations, a working directory, and `dryRun`. Each `write-file` operation sets `ifExists` to `error` (default), `skip`, or `overwrite`. It returns written and skipped paths. The service resolves the real path of the nearest existing path and rejects a target that escapes the configured root, including through an existing symlink. A dangling symlink (one whose destination does not exist yet) is not detected, and `write-file` follows it, so do not scaffold into directories that untrusted parties can write to.

```ts
import { createScaffold } from "@clifn/core/scaffold";

const result = await createScaffold().apply([
  { kind: "mkdir", path: "src" },
  { kind: "write-file", path: "src/index.ts", content: "export {};\n", ifExists: "skip" },
], { cwd: process.cwd(), dryRun: false });
console.log({ written: result.written, skipped: result.skipped });
```

With `dryRun`, `apply()` writes nothing and returns the planned `written` and `skipped` paths; it does not print them, so display the result yourself before applying it. `ScaffoldError` carries `CLIFN_SCAFFOLD_EXISTS` or `CLIFN_SCAFFOLD_INVALID_PATH`.

---

<!-- page:docs:cli-builder.md path:/docs/cli-builder -->
# Build a CLI

> Wire any parser to the shared action runner and preserve command ownership.


`runAction(action, options, runnerOptions)` executes a parsed action and returns a numeric exit code. Pass the parser's resolved options to it; keep command names, flags, validation, and help text in your CLI package. Parser packages remain consumer dependencies.

```ts
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const { values, positionals } = parseArgs({
  allowPositionals: true,
  options: {
    name: { type: "string" },
    json: { type: "boolean" },
  },
});

if (positionals[0] === "greet") {
  process.exitCode = await runAction(
    ({ name }, ctx) => {
      if (ctx.output.mode !== "json") ctx.output.info(`Hello, ${name}!`);
      return { data: { greeting: `Hello, ${name}!` } };
    },
    { name: values.name ?? "world" },
    { mode: values.json ? "json" : "text" },
  );
}
```

In text mode, emit user-facing messages with `ctx.output`. In JSON mode, returned `data` is serialized to stdout. `RunnerOptions` accepts `mode` (`"text"` or `"json"`) along with `quiet`, `verbose`, `color`, `cwd`, `env`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `nonInteractive`, and an `onDiagnostics` listener. The context's `exec` and `scaffold` services inherit its working directory; `exec` also inherits its environment.

Return `exitCode` for an expected product failure you have handled. An invalid or negative returned exit code normalizes to zero, so set explicit positive codes for failure cases. Thrown failures normalize to code 1. The runner does not print collected diagnostics automatically; use `onDiagnostics` or your own output policy to present them.

See the [runner source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/core/src/runner.ts) and [package examples](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md) for `commander` and `cac` integration.

---

<!-- page:docs:configuration.md path:/docs/configuration -->
# Configuration

> Load local config files, JSON project settings, and typed environment values.


CliFn has separate facilities for a discovered config module, a simple JSON project config store, and environment variables. Choose the one that fits the lifecycle of the consuming CLI.

## Discover a config file

`loadConfig()` searches `config.ts`, `config.js`, `config.mjs`, `config.cjs`, then `config.json` by default. Pass `configPath` for an explicit file, `candidates` for a custom search, `exportNames` for named module exports, and `validate` for a typed value. The result includes both `config` and the resolved `path`.

```ts
import { loadConfig } from "@clifn/core/config-loader";

const loaded = await loadConfig<{ target: string }>({
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  validate(value) {
    if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || !("target" in value)) {
      throw new Error("target is required");
    }
    return value as { target: string };
  },
});
```

The loader accepts local TS, JS, MJS, CJS, and JSON files. TS uses Jiti. Module exports may be direct values, functions, or promises. Remote URLs and unsupported extensions are rejected; failures use `CLIFN_CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `CLIFN_CONFIG_INVALID`, or `CLIFN_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED`. A custom candidate list is limited to 32 entries. `defineConfig()` is an identity helper for typed authoring.

## Store project settings

`createProjectConfig(path?)` provides a JSON store with `read`, `write`, `get`, and `set`. Pass `{ appName: "my-cli", fileName? }` for `<config>/config.json` from `resolveAppPaths` (`@clifn/core/paths`), `{ cwd?, fileName }` for a project-local file, or a product-specific path (`{ path }` is the same as the string); `fileName` must stay inside its directory, and malformed options raise `InvalidStoreOptionsError`. The legacy default is `conduct.config.json` in `process.cwd()`, resolved once when the module is first loaded. Invalid JSON or a non-object shape raises `InvalidConfigError`. It is separate from the discovered module loader.

## Read environment values

`@clifn/core/env` exports `readRequiredStringEnv`, `readStringEnv`, `readIntEnv`, and `readBooleanEnv`. Each accepts an injected `env` map for tests. Defaults, empty-string rules, and integer `min`/`max` are explicit. Errors have `CLIFN_ENV_MISSING`, `CLIFN_ENV_INVALID`, or `CLIFN_ENV_OUT_OF_RANGE` codes. See the [export reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/exports.md) for option types.

---

<!-- page:docs:credentials-and-client.md path:/docs/credentials-and-client -->
# Credentials and HTTP client

> Persist named profiles and make authenticated requests with bounded retries.


`createCredentialStore(path?)` stores named `{ backend, key }` profiles in an INI file. Pass `{ appName: "my-cli" }` to store them at `<config>/credentials` from `resolveAppPaths` (`@clifn/core/paths`), or a product-specific path (`{ path }` is the same as the string); the legacy default is `~/.conduct/credentials`. The synchronous store supports `getProfile`, `setProfile`, `hasProfile`, `removeProfile`, and `listProfiles`. A missing profile raises `MissingProfileError`.

Credential writes use a sibling lock, a mode-0600 temporary file, fsync, and atomic rename. A write that cannot take the lock throws a plain `Error` whose message is `CLIFN_CREDENTIAL_STORE_BUSY` (there is no `code` property, so match on `error.message`). A writer that crashes while holding the lock leaves the sibling `.lock` file behind, and every later write fails the same way until it is removed: stop all writers, then delete only that `.lock` file before retrying. A credentials path that is a symlink to an existing file is rejected with an `Error` whose message is `CLIFN_CREDENTIAL_SYMLINK`; a dangling symlink is treated as a missing file, and the next write replaces the link itself with a regular file. Filesystem permissions are a fallback, not encryption or an OS keychain. For keychain integration, inject a `CredentialStore` implementation and persist values before reporting success.

## Make a request

```ts
import { createApiClient } from "@clifn/core/client";
import { createCredentialStore } from "@clifn/core/credentials";
import { homedir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const credentials = createCredentialStore(join(homedir(), ".my-cli", "credentials"));
// A fresh file has no profiles; save one (for example from a login command) first.
if (!credentials.hasProfile("default")) {
  const key = process.env.MY_CLI_API_KEY;
  if (!key) throw new Error("Set MY_CLI_API_KEY or run the login command first");
  credentials.setProfile("default", { backend: "https://api.example.com", key });
}

const client = createApiClient({
  credentials,
  profile: "default",
  projectId: "example",
});

const response = await client.get<{ items: unknown[] }>("/items", { limit: 20 });
console.log(response.data);
```

The profile is resolved when the client is constructed, so a missing profile throws `MissingProfileError` from `createApiClient()`. Alternatively pass `{ baseUrl, apiKey }` directly and skip the credential store. The client adds Bearer authorization unless the request sets its own authorization header, and adds `X-Project-ID` when configured. Paths must be relative. Responses include status, parsed data, and headers. Non-2xx responses throw `HttpFailureError`; transport failures throw `HttpRequestError`.

Only GET requests retry by default, on HTTP 429 or 5xx and retryable transport failures. Use `request({ ..., retrySafe: true })` only when the server guarantees idempotency. One-shot stream bodies are not retried. A timed-out write may already have succeeded, so reconcile before repeating it. `ApiClientConfig` accepts `retries`, `retryDelayMs`, `timeoutMs`, `defaultHeaders`, and `fetchImpl`.

---

<!-- page:docs:getting-started.md path:/docs/getting-started -->
# Getting started

> Install CliFn and run your first parser-independent action.


## Install

```sh
npm install @clifn/core
```

CliFn is a toolkit, not an executable or parser. Keep your existing command registration in `commander`, `cac`, `node:util.parseArgs`, or another parser. Import the pieces you need by public subpath.

## Run an action

```ts
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const exitCode = await runAction(
  async ({ name }, ctx) => {
    ctx.output.info(`hello ${name}`);
  },
  { name: "world" },
  { mode: "text" },
);

process.exitCode = exitCode;
```

`runAction()` provides a normalized working directory, environment, output service, diagnostic sink, subprocess service, scaffold service, and `nonInteractive` flag. An action can return `exitCode`, `data`, and diagnostics; thrown errors become exit code 1. JSON mode emits a stable `CLIFN_RUNNER_FAILED` envelope; text mode writes the failure message. In JSON mode, returned `data` is emitted as JSON. See [CLI builder](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/cli-builder.md) for parser wiring and [output and diagnostics](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/output-and-diagnostics.md) for formatting.

The [package README](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md) contains working examples for `commander`, `cac`, and raw `parseArgs`, along with the established compatibility imports.

---

<!-- page:docs:index.md path:/docs -->
# CliFn documentation

> Build reliable command-line tools with parser-agnostic primitives.


`@clifn/core` is a Node.js toolkit for the concerns that recur across command-line applications. It supplies an action runner, text and JSON output, configuration and environment readers, credential storage, an authenticated HTTP client, prompts, JSON stdio, subprocess execution, scaffolding, and diagnostics. Your CLI owns its commands, parser, and product behavior.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md): install the package and run an action.
- [Build a CLI](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/cli-builder.md): connect your parser to `runAction()` and set exit status.
- [Output and diagnostics](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/output-and-diagnostics.md): human and machine-readable results.
- [Configuration](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/configuration.md): config modules, JSON project settings, and environment values.
- [Credentials and HTTP](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/credentials-and-client.md): profile persistence and safe request retries.
- [Automation](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/automation.md): subprocesses and bounded file generation.
- [Interaction and stdio](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/interaction-and-stdio.md): prompts, terminal helpers, and JSON pipes.

## Public entry points

Import from documented subpaths such as `@clifn/core/runner`, `@clifn/core/output`, or `@clifn/core/credentials`. The [export reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/exports.md) lists all thirteen public subpaths and their principal functions and types. `@clifn/core` itself also exports the shared surface. Avoid importing internal `dist/*` paths.

---

<!-- page:docs:interaction-and-stdio.md path:/docs/interaction-and-stdio -->
# Prompts and JSON stdio

> Interactive input, terminal feedback, and machine-readable pipes.


`@clifn/core/prompt` exports the named, preconfigured `prompt` object and `createPrompt()` for an injected ask function. It supports `select`, `multiSelect`, `text`, and `confirm`. Use the runner's `nonInteractive` flag to decide whether your command should prompt or require flags; the prompt API itself does not infer that policy. Invalid answers throw `PromptInputError` (code `CLIFN_PROMPT_INPUT_ERROR`): `confirm` accepts only y, yes, n, or no; `select` and `multiSelect` accept a listed choice or its 1-based number and also throw for an empty choice list.

```ts
import { prompt } from "@clifn/core/prompt";
import { ui } from "@clifn/core/ui";

// Inside a runAction handler; `targetFlag` comes from your parsed options.
const targets = ["local", "staging"];
const target = ctx.nonInteractive
  ? targets.find((choice) => choice === targetFlag)
  : await prompt.select("Target environment", targets);
if (!target) throw new Error("--target must be one of local, staging in non-interactive mode");
if (ctx.nonInteractive || (await prompt.confirm(`Continue with ${target}?`))) {
  ui.success(`selected ${target}`);
}
```

`@clifn/core/ui` retains the established `success`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `spinner`, and `table` terminal helpers. For new CLI output policies, prefer the configurable `createOutput()` service described in [output and diagnostics](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/output-and-diagnostics.md).

`@clifn/core/stdio` exports `readJsonStdin<T>()` and `writeJsonStdout(value)`. The reader parses one JSON document from stdin and raises `InvalidJsonStdinError` on malformed input. The writer emits one serialized JSON document followed by a newline. Both accept injected streams for testing. Keep progress and human messages off stdout when a command promises machine-readable output.

---

<!-- page:docs:output-and-diagnostics.md path:/docs/output-and-diagnostics -->
# Output and diagnostics

> Use text or JSON output and stable, redacted diagnostic reports.


`createOutput()` supplies `debug`, `info`, `success`, `warn`, `error`, `json`, `table`, and `spinner`. Use `@clifn/core/output` for new CLIs; `@clifn/core/ui` remains the compatibility terminal helper path.

```ts
import { createOutput } from "@clifn/core/output";

const output = createOutput({ mode: "json", quiet: false });
output.info("loading");
output.json({ ok: true, count: 3 });
```

In text mode, messages have stable level prefixes; errors go to stderr. In JSON mode, messages become one JSON record per line and spinners do nothing. `quiet` suppresses non-error messages and tables; `debug` requires `verbose`. `json(value)` writes a JSON line directly. Tables use explicit columns and deterministic row order supplied by the caller. Inject `stdout` and `stderr` callbacks for tests or embedding.

## Diagnostics

`@clifn/core/diagnostics` defines `Diagnostic` with `code`, `severity`, `message`, optional `path`, and optional `details`. Use `createDiagnostic`, `sortDiagnostics`, `redactDiagnostics`, `formatDiagnosticsText`, and `formatDiagnosticsJson` to build consistent reports.

```ts
import {
  createDiagnostic,
  formatDiagnosticsJson,
  redactDiagnostics,
} from "@clifn/core/diagnostics";

const diagnostics = [createDiagnostic({
  code: "INPUT_MISSING",
  severity: "error",
  message: "A target is required",
})];
process.stdout.write(formatDiagnosticsJson(redactDiagnostics(diagnostics)));
```

Redaction applies to diagnostic `details`; applications should still avoid putting credentials in messages or paths. Formatters sort diagnostics and add a trailing newline. Consult the [export reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/exports.md) for types and the [source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/core/src/diagnostics.ts) for redaction rules.

<!-- page:docs:reference/admin.md path:/docs/reference/admin -->
# Admin capability

> The current Super Console declaration for CliFn.


`@clifn/admin` exports `cliFnAdminCapability`, `cliFnAdminAdapter`, and their `adminCapability` and `adminAdapter` aliases for Super Console registration. Its capability is declared **unavailable** and has no operations. CliFn currently provides local CLI process utilities; it has no durable server-side operator service or remote authorization boundary.

Do not expose credential files, local command execution, or scaffolding as remote admin actions. Consumers building command-line tools should use `@clifn/core` directly. See the [admin source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/admin/src/index.ts) for the declared schema version, installation scope, and availability reason.

---

<!-- page:docs:reference/core-readme.md path:/docs/reference/core-readme -->
# Package README

> Complete source-aligned CliFn package guide.


Reusable CLI primitives for Superfunctions packages and downstream CLIs.

`clifn` remains a single package at `clifn/core`, published as `@clifn/core`. It is the shared parser-agnostic CLI toolkit for generic concerns that repeat across Superfunctions CLIs, while each owning CLI keeps its product-specific command graph and behavior.

Current public subpaths:

- `@clifn/core/credentials`
- `@clifn/core/config`
- `@clifn/core/client`
- `@clifn/core/ui`
- `@clifn/core/stdio`
- `@clifn/core/prompt`

New additive subpaths are exported for the generic CLI-builder surface:

- `@clifn/core/output`
- `@clifn/core/runner`
- `@clifn/core/config-loader`
- `@clifn/core/env`
- `@clifn/core/diagnostics`
- `@clifn/core/exec`
- `@clifn/core/scaffold`
- `@clifn/core/paths`
- `@clifn/core/terminal`

## Install

```bash
npm install @clifn/core
```

## Conduct CLI-style usage

```ts
import { createCredentialStore } from "@clifn/core/credentials";
import { createProjectConfig } from "@clifn/core/config";
import { createApiClient } from "@clifn/core/client";
import { readJsonStdin, writeJsonStdout } from "@clifn/core/stdio";

const credentials = createCredentialStore();
const config = createProjectConfig();
const profile = String(config.get("profile") ?? "default");

const api = createApiClient({
  credentials,
  profile,
  projectId: String(config.get("projectId") ?? ""),
});

const input = await readJsonStdin<{ command: string }>();
process.stderr.write(`running command: ${input.command}\n`);
const result = await api.post("/runs", input);
writeJsonStdout(result.data);
```

## Generic CLI usage

```ts
import { prompt } from "@clifn/core/prompt";
import { ui } from "@clifn/core/ui";

const target = await prompt.select("Target environment", [
  "local",
  "staging",
  "production",
]);
const confirmed = await prompt.confirm(`Deploy to ${target}?`);

if (!confirmed) {
  ui.warn("deployment cancelled");
} else {
  ui.success(`deployment started for ${target}`);
}
```

## Shared CLI-builder quick start

```ts
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const exitCode = await runAction(
  async ({ name }, ctx) => {
    ctx.output.info(`hello ${name}`);
  },
  { name: "world" },
  {
    verbose: false,
  }
);

process.exitCode = exitCode;
```

## Parser compatibility patterns

`clifn` stays parser-agnostic. The owning CLI keeps parser choice and parser dependencies, while `clifn` supplies the reusable execution and output primitives underneath.

The current repository already uses all three parser styles:

- `hostfn/cli`, `plugfn/cli`, and `extfn/cli` use `commander`
- `apifn/cli` uses `cac`
- `datafn/cli` uses raw `node:util.parseArgs`

The parser canaries under `clifn/core/tests/fixtures/*` prove that `runAction()` and the shared output service work in each style without adding parser libraries to `clifn` runtime dependencies.

### `commander`

```ts
import { Command } from "commander";
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const program = new Command();

program.option("--json", "Emit machine-readable output");
program
  .command("greet")
  .option("--name <name>", "Name to greet", "world")
  .action(async (options, command) => {
    const globals = command.parent?.opts() ?? {};

    process.exitCode = await runAction(
      async ({ name }, ctx) => {
        ctx.output.info(`hello ${name}`);
      },
      { name: options.name },
      {
        mode: globals.json ? "json" : "text",
      }
    );
  });

await program.parseAsync(process.argv);
```

### `cac`

```ts
import { cac } from "cac";
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const cli = cac("demo");

cli.option("--json", "Emit machine-readable output");
cli
  .command("greet")
  .option("--name <name>", "Name to greet")
  .action(async (options) => {
    process.exitCode = await runAction(
      async ({ name }, ctx) => {
        return {
          data: {
            ok: true,
            name,
          },
        };
      },
      { name: options.name ?? "world" },
      {
        mode: options.json ? "json" : "text",
      }
    );
  });

cli.parse(process.argv, { run: false });
await cli.runMatchedCommand();
```

### `node:util.parseArgs`

```ts
import { parseArgs } from "node:util";
import { runAction } from "@clifn/core/runner";

const { values, positionals } = parseArgs({
  allowPositionals: true,
  options: {
    name: { type: "string" },
    json: { type: "boolean" },
  },
});

if (positionals[0] === "greet") {
  process.exitCode = await runAction(
    async ({ name }, ctx) => {
      ctx.output.info(`hello ${name}`);
    },
    { name: values.name ?? "world" },
    {
      mode: values.json ? "json" : "text",
    }
  );
}
```

Consumer ownership stays explicit:

- `clifn` owns the parser-agnostic runner/output/diagnostics/config/env/exec/scaffold helpers
- the consuming CLI owns command registration, parser wiring, and parser package installation
- parser libraries such as `commander` and `cac` remain consumer dependencies or test-only canary dependencies, not `clifn` runtime dependencies

## API Overview

### Compatibility promise

- Existing imports for `@clifn/core/credentials`, `@clifn/core/config`, `@clifn/core/client`, `@clifn/core/ui`, `@clifn/core/stdio`, and `@clifn/core/prompt` remain valid.
- The new subpaths are additive and do not replace any existing import path.
- `@clifn/core/ui` remains the compatibility-facing terminal helper path even as newer shared output primitives land in `@clifn/core/output`.

### `@clifn/core/credentials`

- `createCredentialStore(path?)` -> INI profile store.
- `createCredentialStore({ appName })` -> the same store at `<config>/credentials` from `resolveAppPaths(appName)`; `{ path }` equals the string form. Without an argument the Conduct default `~/.conduct/credentials` stays.
- `MissingProfileError` -> typed error when profile is not found.

### `@clifn/core/config`

- `createProjectConfig(path?)` -> JSON project config store.
- `createProjectConfig({ appName, fileName? })` -> `<config>/<fileName>` (default `config.json`); `{ cwd?, fileName }` -> a project-local file; `{ path }` equals the string form. Without an argument the Conduct default `conduct.config.json` stays.
- `{ appName }` stores resolve only the config directory for the current platform (`env` and `homedir` may be passed through, a different `platform` throws); `fileName` must stay inside its directory. Only own properties of the options object are read (enumerable or not; inherited keys are ignored). The selector of the form (`appName`, `path`, or `fileName` for a project-local file) must be a string, and an optional key set to `undefined` (`fileName` beside `appName`, `cwd`, `env`, `homedir`) takes its default. A selector set to `undefined` or a non-string, a key from another form, or an unknown key throws `InvalidStoreOptionsError` (`CLIFN_INVALID_STORE_OPTIONS`) instead of falling back to another form or the Conduct default. Every own property descriptor is captured before any getter runs, and each getter is called once. An object-form target must name a file: `{ path: "" }`, a path ending in a separator or a root (`C:\`, `\\server\share`), `.` or `..`, and a NUL character in `path`, `fileName` or `cwd` throw `InvalidStoreOptionsError` before any filesystem call; the string form is used as given. `fileName` cannot start with a drive (`C:`) before or after normalization (`./C:x`). On Windows no `fileName` segment, and not the base name of an object-form target, may contain `:`, be a device name (`nul`, `CON.json`) or end with a dot or space, since Windows would open a device or another name. Loading the module does not fail when the home or working directory is unavailable; the no-argument defaults are still taken at import when they can be.
- `InvalidConfigError` -> typed error for invalid JSON/object shapes.

### `@clifn/core/client`

- `createApiClient(config)` -> authenticated HTTP client with retries.
- `HttpFailureError` -> typed error for non-2xx responses.
- `HttpRequestError` -> typed error for network/transport failures.

### `@clifn/core/ui`

- `ui.success`, `ui.error`, `ui.warn`, `ui.info`
- `ui.spinner(message)` -> start/stop/succeed/fail
- `ui.table(rows)` -> deterministic table output

### `@clifn/core/stdio`

- `readJsonStdin<T>()` -> parse one JSON document from stdin.
- `writeJsonStdout(value)` -> serialize one JSON document + trailing newline.
- `InvalidJsonStdinError` -> typed deterministic parse failure.

### `@clifn/core/prompt`

- `prompt.select`
- `prompt.multiSelect`
- `prompt.text`
- `prompt.confirm`
- `createPrompt({ ask?, output?, nonInteractive? })`: with `nonInteractive: true` every prompt throws `PromptInputError` with code `CLIFN_PROMPT_NON_INTERACTIVE`; an options object that names `output` or `nonInteractive` writes questions to `output`, else stderr. `createPrompt()`, `createPrompt({ ask })` and `prompt` keep writing to stdout.

### New shared CLI-builder modules

These module entrypoints are the generic surface that repository CLIs can share:

- `@clifn/core/output`
  - generic text/JSON output service contract
  - quiet/verbose behavior
  - deterministic table rendering
  - spinner surface
- `@clifn/core/runner`
  - parser-agnostic action runner contract
  - normalized action context with output, diagnostics, exec, scaffold, cwd, env, and non-interactive state
  - `jsonStyle: 'document'` with `mode: 'json'` (D8) prints exactly one newline-terminated JSON document on stdout, on success or failure: `{"ok":true,"data":...}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code","message","details"?}}`, with `diagnostics` only when there are any. Every log level, and a spinner's `succeed`/`fail` message, is a JSON line on stderr (`quiet` and `verbose` apply as in JSON lines), and streamed child output (`exec.command(file, args, { streamOutput: true })`) goes to stderr unless that command passes its own `stdout`/`stderr` writer. `output.json()` and `output.table()` are collected: when the action returns no `data`, the last `json` value becomes `data`; absent data, or data JSON leaves out, prints `null`; a stderr warning names each call that was not used. Leaving `jsonStyle` out keeps JSON lines, and text mode is unchanged
  - document error codes and exit codes follow the CLI-12 classification: a string `code` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63}$`, else a message that is exactly `CLIFN_...` (with a fixed description), else `CLIFN_RUNNER_FAILED`; the exit code is an integer `exitCode` from 1 to 125, else 1. Plain-object `details` (with a null prototype or the `Object.prototype` of any realm, such as a `vm` context) are kept when they serialize to a JSON object and left out otherwise; a diagnostic whose code or message is not a string, whose severity is not `error`, `warning` or `info`, or that cannot be serialized, is left out with a fixed stderr warning
  - document redaction is key-based on the emitted structure: in `data` (including the `json()` fallback), error `details` and diagnostic `details`, every object key matching the sensitive-key pattern (`authorization`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, `cookie`, `api key`, `session id`, `access key`, `refresh token`, case-insensitive, with or without `-`/`_`) or `DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG` prints `"[REDACTED]"`. Keys are matched after each `toJSON` runs, so keys a projection creates are covered. Messages (thrown, diagnostic and log) print as given, and a custom `toJSON` that renames a sensitive key (`password` to `pw`) or puts a secret under an unrelated key prints what it returns: callers supply safe messages and safe projections. Redaction covers the stdout document only: stderr log lines print their message and `details` as given, as in JSON lines
  - document bounds: values are serialized in one pass that follows `JSON.stringify` (each member, getter and `toJSON` is read or run once, in native order); bigints print as strings, an object already being serialized prints `"[Circular]"`, and a `toJSON` that keeps projecting back to the same value for the same member key is cut with `"[Circular]"` after 64 nested projections for that key; projections for other keys (a finite sibling of the cut branch) print in full, at any depth and in any member order, and a `toJSON` that keeps branching back to itself under several keys fails on the bounds below. A document is at most the smaller of the engine's maximum string length and a sixteenth of V8's heap limit, in characters including its newline; a redacted value costs only its key and placeholder, and work has its own allowance of twice the document's characters: each own key of each object as it is listed (printed, left out, skipped by JSON such as a non-enumerable or symbol key, or under a redacted key; never given back, also when the object then fails, so listing the same object again and again stops), each array item walked under a redacted key, each scan of text found too long to print, each character of details or a diagnostic written and then left out, and 32 units per typed-array index; a document that fits lists at most a quarter of its characters in printed keys, so it prints next to that work; a sensitive key is matched only once its member prints. An array longer than the room left fails before its first item is read, a typed array is bounded by its length before its keys are listed (redacted or not), a `Buffer` projected by Node's built-in `toJSON` is read in place and bounded like an array by its length once its key's redaction is known (a Proxy, a receiver that is not a typed array or a shadowed `length` fails instead of being copied), a bigint is checked by size before it is converted and never converted under a redacted key, and nesting deeper than 512 levels fails; only one key list of an object is held, and the key lists of the objects open on the path may hold a quarter of the document's characters in keys together, at least 65,536 (a document whose members all print never comes near it, and a redacted subtree below that count is bounded by the work allowance alone), so an object nested below lists that hold more fails before its own keys are listed, even by a Proxy's `ownKeys` trap; the engine takes a Proxy's key list (from its `ownKeys` trap, or its target's keys for a Proxy without that trap) before it can be charged, after which its descriptors are charged like any other keys. A result whose `data`, `exitCode` or `diagnostics` getter throws prints the same fixed document; a returned diagnostic that cannot be read (a throwing index getter, a failing iterator, a value that is not a list; a string or other primitive is never iterated) is left out with a warning while its siblings, the data and the exit code are kept; each diagnostic is written once, when it is added or returned (each member read once, its details through their `toJSON`), and the run keeps that redacted text, never the object it was given, so a later change to the object is not printed; `ctx.diagnostics.list()` and `onDiagnostics` (called once) receive copies parsed from the text, redacted as the document prints them, without the entries that could not be read or printed, and the listener's throw after a successful action is the run's failure. What a run keeps for its diagnostics is bounded by the document limit: their text by what a document can print after its smallest data, and the work of writing them by its own allowance of twice the limit (a string left out for size costs its length, at most the limit); reading returned or added diagnostics stops once nothing more can be kept. A diagnostic added while another is being written (from its getter or `toJSON`) is dropped with a warning, so it cannot spend the budget the diagnostic being written reserved. The listed copies always carry the code, severity, message and path; their details are parsed only while 32 units per character of details text fit an allowance of the limit (about the document's size in bytes), and past it a diagnostic is listed without details, though the document still prints them. Data that does not fit or cannot be serialized prints the fixed `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"CLIFN_RUNNER_FAILED","message":"Unable to serialize the result document"}}` (exit 1); error details that do not fit are left out and an error message that does not fit is replaced by a fixed one, keeping the code and exit code; diagnostics that do not fit after the data or error are left out with a warning, and a kept diagnostic whose details alone do not fit prints without them. A thrown value's code, message (or `name`) and exit code are read and classified before its `details`, so a details getter or projection cannot change them. The fixed failure document and the stderr warnings the runner writes are fixed text (`{"level":"warn","message":...}` lines), so nothing inherited such as an `Object.prototype.toJSON` changes them. Stderr warnings and streamed child output without its own writer are advisory: at most 20 warnings per kind plus one summary line, and a stderr writer that throws on them does not change the document or the exit code; a code longer than 64 characters, or a message longer than the document, is never scanned as a code
- `@clifn/core/config-loader`
  - shared config discovery and typed loading contract for TS/JS/MJS/CJS/JSON configs
  - uses the same Jiti-informed `.ts` loading path already established in `packages/cli` and `apifn/cli`
- `@clifn/core/env`
  - generic environment readers for strings, integers, and booleans
  - explicit missing, invalid, and out-of-range error codes for shared CLI callers
- `@clifn/core/diagnostics`
  - shared diagnostic model plus deterministic sort/redaction/formatting surface
- `@clifn/core/exec`
  - subprocess execution contract for buffered capture, streaming, and timeout reporting
- `@clifn/core/scaffold`
  - deterministic file and directory scaffolding contract with explicit overwrite policy
- `@clifn/core/paths`
  - `resolveAppPaths(appName, { platform?, env?, homedir? })` -> `{ config, state, cache }`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (else `~/.config`, `~/.local/state`, `~/.cache`) followed by `/<app>` on Linux, macOS and other POSIX platforms; `%APPDATA%\<app>` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\State` / `\Cache` on Windows (else `<home>\AppData\Roaming` / `Local`)
  - environment values count only when they are absolute paths (a UNC path needs a real server and share; device and extended-length `\\.\` / `\\?\` paths are not used, and the home directory follows the same rule); relative or empty values, and values containing a NUL character, use the defaults, and only a default reads the home directory (a home directory containing a NUL is invalid)
  - app names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, else `InvalidAppNameError` (`CLIFN_INVALID_APP_NAME`); on Windows (`platform: "win32"`, and the stores on Windows) a name also cannot end with `.` (Windows drops it, so `tool.` would share `tool`'s directories) or be a device name (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com0`-`com9`, `lpt0`-`lpt9`), with or without an extension (`nul.txt`)
  - `ensureAppDir(dir)` creates a missing directory with mode `0o700` on POSIX and resolves to `dir`; concurrent calls on one path both resolve
  - symlinks or directories that another program plants under these paths are not defended against yet
- `@clifn/core/terminal`
  - `resolveTerminal({ env?, stdin?, stdout?, stderr?, json? })` -> `{ color, interactive, ci }`: a non-empty `NO_COLOR` disables colour; `FORCE_COLOR` `0`/`false` disables and `1`/`2`/`3`/`true` enables it; `TERM=dumb` disables it; otherwise colour follows whether stderr is a TTY. `ci` is `CI` set to anything but empty, `0` or `false`; `interactive` needs TTY stdin and stderr, no CI and no JSON
  - `resolveRunnerOptions({ json?, quiet?, verbose?, color?, yes?, nonInteractive? }, { env?, streams? })` -> runner options (`mode`, `'json'` with `jsonStyle: 'document'` for `json`; `color`, `stderrColor`, `quiet`, `verbose`, `nonInteractive`) from the flags your parser produced; `color: true`/`false` overrides the rules and `'auto'` uses them; `stderrColor` (errors, spinner) follows the rules and, in text mode, `color` (`info`, `success` and `warn` on stdout) also needs a TTY stdout unless `FORCE_COLOR` enables it (commander and cac give a lone `--no-color` a default of `true`, so pass `color: opts.color === false ? false : 'auto'`)

## Adoption boundary

`clifn` is the shared home for generic CLI-builder concerns that appear across existing repository CLIs such as:

- `packages/cli` and `apifn/cli` for config loading patterns
- `hostfn/cli`, `plugfn/cli`, and `apifn/cli` for output and command-runner patterns
- `plugfn/cli` and `mcpfn/cli` for structured diagnostics and test/reporting surfaces

Responsibilities that belong in `clifn`:

- generic action execution
- generic output formatting and machine-readable output
- config discovery/loading contracts
- generic env readers
- generic diagnostics formatting
- generic subprocess helpers
- generic scaffolding helpers

Responsibilities that stay in the owning CLI:

- product-specific command graphs
- business/domain validation
- domain-specific scan rules
- deployment or packaging rules tied to one product
- browser-extension orchestration and manifest-aware behavior

## Representative adoption notes

### `packages/cli`

- Repeated pattern today:
  - config discovery and loading in `packages/cli/src/utils/load-library-config.ts`
  - config-path fallback logic in `packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`
- `clifn` adoption target:
  - `@clifn/core/config-loader` for deterministic TS/JS/MJS/CJS/JSON loading
- Product-owned concerns that stay local:
  - schema and library semantics specific to `@superfunctions/cli`

### `apifn/cli`

- Repeated pattern today:
  - `cac` command registration in `apifn/cli/src/index.ts`
  - config loading in `apifn/cli/src/config.ts`
  - output helpers in `apifn/cli/src/utils/output.ts`
- `clifn` adoption target:
  - keep `cac`, but move generic concerns onto `@clifn/core/runner`, `@clifn/core/output`, and `@clifn/core/config-loader`
- Product-owned concerns that stay local:
  - OpenAPI generation, diff semantics, mock/serve behavior, and collection rules

### `hostfn/cli`

- Repeated pattern today:
  - `commander` command registration and repeated async `try/catch` wrappers in `hostfn/cli/src/index.ts`
  - logger formatting in `hostfn/cli/src/utils/logger.ts`
- `clifn` adoption target:
  - keep `commander`, but move shared action execution and output concerns onto `@clifn/core/runner`, `@clifn/core/output`, and `@clifn/core/exec`
- Product-owned concerns that stay local:
  - deployment workflows, SSH/server orchestration, runtime adapters, and host-specific validation

### `plugfn/cli`

- Repeated pattern today:
  - text/json rendering in `plugfn/cli/src/commands/runtime.ts`
  - structured diagnostics in `plugfn/cli/src/commands/test.ts`
- `clifn` adoption target:
  - `@clifn/core/output` for generic mode switching and transport
  - `@clifn/core/diagnostics` for stable diagnostic formatting
  - keep domain-specific formatters local where they encode provider/runtime semantics
- Product-owned concerns that stay local:
  - provider diagnostics, webhook fixtures, and integration-specific data shapes

### extfn adoption contract

`extfn/cli` is an explicit future adopter of the generic `clifn` surface, but only for generic CLI concerns.

`extfn/cli` SHOULD use:

- `@clifn/core/runner` for normalized action execution and exit handling
- `@clifn/core/output` for text/json output, quiet/verbose behavior, and spinner usage
- `@clifn/core/diagnostics` for stable formatting and redaction of generic diagnostics
- `@clifn/core/config-loader` for extension config discovery and loading
- `@clifn/core/env` for generic env parsing
- `@clifn/core/exec` for subprocess orchestration during builds and packaging
- `@clifn/core/scaffold` for template-free deterministic file creation

`extfn/cli` MAY keep:

- its preferred parser (`commander`, `cac`, or raw `parseArgs`)
- product-specific formatter helpers that encode extension semantics

`extfn/cli` MUST stay extfn-owned for:

- Vite-based extension orchestration
- browser launching behavior
- extension packaging rules and archive layout
- manifest-aware scan rules
- plugin-specific contracts such as extension plugin wiring
- target-specific extension validation

If `extfn/cli` needs a generic capability that is not yet exported by `clifn`, that capability should be added to `clifn` first instead of being reimplemented as extfn-local CLI infrastructure.

## Notes

- Package path follows repo convention: `clifn/core` workspace, package name `@clifn/core`.
- `clifn` is designed for public imports only; no private/internal path imports are required.
- The generic modules prefer repository-shared mechanisms, including the existing `packages/cli` loader pattern, before introducing new runtime dependencies.
- `@clifn/core/config-loader` rejects remote config URLs and unsupported extensions with explicit error codes.
- `@clifn/core/env` uses explicit `CLIFN_ENV_*` error codes for missing, invalid, and out-of-range values.

## Conduct v0.3 compatibility note

`clifn` intentionally exposes stable subpath imports for Conduct and other CLIs:

- `@clifn/core/credentials`
- `@clifn/core/config`
- `@clifn/core/client`
- `@clifn/core/ui`
- `@clifn/core/stdio`
- `@clifn/core/prompt`

Use these public subpaths directly; do not import from internal `dist/*` paths.

## Application credentials and safe retry defaults

Pass `{ appName }` (or an explicit path) to `createCredentialStore` for each product so it stores credentials in its own config directory; the legacy no-argument default remains Conduct-specific. Writes hold an exclusive sibling `.lock`, write and fsync a unique mode-0600 temporary file, then rename it atomically. Concurrent writes fail with `CLIFN_CREDENTIAL_STORE_BUSY` rather than losing updates. After a process crash, stop all writers and inspect/remove only its stale lock before retrying. Symlink credential files are rejected. Filesystem permissions are a fallback, not encryption or an OS keychain.

The synchronous `CredentialStore` interface is injectable into `createApiClient`. A consumer keychain adapter should use a product-specific service name and profile account, store each complete `{backend,key}` value atomically, and expose only profile names in diagnostics. An asynchronous OS keychain can be loaded at CLI startup into a short-lived in-memory implementation; persist changes through the keychain before reporting success. Never serialize keychain values to a config file as an implicit fallback.

Only GET requests retry by default. `request({ ..., retrySafe: true })` opts in when the server guarantees idempotency for that operation; it does not manufacture such a guarantee. Non-replayable request bodies are not retried. A timed-out write may already have succeeded and must be reconciled.

Executable naming belongs to the consumer package.

# Public exports

> Map CliFn subpaths to their public functions, types, and errors.


`@clifn/core` provides these public subpaths. Import from a subpath or the documented package root, never from `dist/*`.

| Subpath | Main exports | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/runner` | `runAction`, `RunnerOptions`, `RunnerJsonStyle`, `RunnerContext`, `RunnerActionResult` | Normalized action execution and exit code; one redacted JSON result document with `jsonStyle: 'document'` |
| `/output` | `createOutput`, `OutputOptions`, `OutputService`, `OutputTable`, `Spinner` | Text and JSON output, tables, spinners |
| `/diagnostics` | `createDiagnostic`, `sortDiagnostics`, `redactDiagnostics`, `formatDiagnosticsText`, `formatDiagnosticsJson`, `Diagnostic` | Stable report formatting and redaction |
| `/config-loader` | `defineConfig`, `loadConfig`, `ConfigLoaderOptions`, `LoadedConfig`, `ConfigLoaderError` | Discover and load TS/JS/MJS/CJS/JSON config |
| `/env` | `readRequiredStringEnv`, `readStringEnv`, `readIntEnv`, `readBooleanEnv`, option types | Typed environment values |
| `/exec` | `createExec`, `ExecOptions`, `ExecResult`, `ExecTimeoutError` | Subprocesses, capture, streams, timeout |
| `/scaffold` | `createScaffold`, `ScaffoldOperation`, `ScaffoldResult`, `ScaffoldError` | Bounded directory and file writes |
| `/credentials` | `createCredentialStore`, `CredentialStore`, `CredentialStoreOptions`, `CredentialProfile`, `MissingProfileError`, `InvalidStoreOptionsError` | Named INI credential profiles, by path or app name |
| `/config` | `createProjectConfig`, `ProjectConfigStore`, `ProjectConfigOptions`, `InvalidConfigError`, `InvalidStoreOptionsError` | JSON project settings, by path, app name or project-local file |
| `/paths` | `resolveAppPaths`, `ensureAppDir`, `AppPaths`, `AppPathsOptions`, `InvalidAppNameError`, `InvalidHomeDirectoryError` | Per-app config, state and cache directories |
| `/terminal` | `resolveTerminal`, `resolveRunnerOptions`, `TerminalState`, `RunnerFlags`, `ResolvedRunnerOptions` | Colour, interactivity and CI rules; global flags to runner options |
| `/client` | `createApiClient`, `ApiClient`, `ApiClientConfig`, `ApiRequestOptions`, `ApiResponse`, HTTP errors | Authenticated HTTP requests |
| `/ui` | `ui`, `Spinner` | Compatibility terminal helpers |
| `/stdio` | `readJsonStdin`, `writeJsonStdout`, `InvalidJsonStdinError` | One-document JSON pipes |
| `/prompt` | `prompt`, `createPrompt`, `PromptApi`, `PromptOptions`, `PromptInputError` | Interactive input; non-interactive prompts throw `CLIFN_PROMPT_NON_INTERACTIVE` |

See the [package export map](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/core/package.json), [source files](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/clifn/core/src), and the task-oriented guides for behavior, defaults, and failure modes.

# API reference

> Public CliFn entry points, exports, and source-aligned package documentation.


- [Public exports](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/exports.md) maps every `@clifn/core/*` subpath to its principal functions, types, and errors.
- [Package README](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md) contains the complete source-aligned usage guide and parser examples.
- [Admin capability](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/admin.md) explains the separate Super Console package and its current availability.

The precise exports for a published release are the versioned package artifact. These pages describe the source on the [`dev` branch](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/clifn/core/src) as of the time the site was prepared.
